title: A Data-Driven Closed-Loop Control Approach to Drive Neural State Transitions for Mechanistic Insight.
reviewer_a_notes: Planning is demonstrated only inside an individually fitted latent model. Region-restricted controls support action sensitivity, but there is no action-agnostic predictive comparator, formal calibration, external cohort, identified causal estimand, or physiological hazard test. Hyperparameters/model selection used test data in a subset.
reviewer_b_notes: Planning is demonstrated only in the learned fMRI model. The controls are simulated and not clinical interventions. Test-segment loss is used to select among five initialized models, and there is no external validation, formal calibration, causal treatment claim, or safety test.

title: A digital twin for hospital antimicrobial resistance forecasting and constrained intervention optimisation
reviewer_a_notes: This is strong within-simulator planning evidence with baseline containment, multiple policy perturbations and constraints. Causal evidence is partial because the estimand and matched random streams are explicit only within an assumed synthetic system; no real-hospital identification or external validation exists. Safety is a constraint/stress proxy, not clinical safety.
reviewer_b_notes: The causal/policy contrast is fully defined inside a known synthetic simulator, hence causal evidence is strong for that simulated data-generating process but does not establish real-hospital effects. The learned predictor is fixed-horizon, not shown consuming its own generated states recursively. Frozen validation is synthetic zero-shot shift.
reviewer_a_anchors: medRxiv v1 Methods: synthetic hospital, H=7 graph forecasting, matched policy branches and MILP; Results report stress tests, held-out action-ranking accuracy/regret/non-worsening; official predictive and causal GitHub repositories.
reviewer_b_anchors: Preprint Methods define the synthetic 10-ward/200-patient/300-staff hospital, T=7/H=7 prediction, partial surveillance, five-policy branch, common deterministic noise, and constrained optimization; Results report surveillance and distribution-shift stress tests and policy ranking; equation defines ΔB7(a)=B7(baseline)-B7(a).

title: DITTO: A Visual Digital Twin for Interventions and Temporal Treatment Outcomes in Head and Neck Cancer.
reviewer_a_notes: Clinician workflow evaluation warrants decision evidence 2, but it is an offline prototype rather than prospective utility. Propensity matching and counterfactual displays provide partial causal evidence without an explicit estimand, overlap checks or complete censoring handling. No public code/data path was located; main text and appendix disagree on total n.
reviewer_b_notes: The accepted manuscript supports retrospective sequential treatment comparison and clinician-facing utility, not prospective planning efficacy. Main text reports 526 patients while Appendix A.2 reports 536=389+147; this discrepancy is retained. Nominal dropout intervals are not empirically calibrated, and no public code, weights, external validation, action-removal test, or hazard test was found.
reviewer_a_anchors: arXiv:2407.13107 pp. 3-4 and Appendix pp. 12-16 describe the cohort, 389/147 split, three treatment stages, transition and survival metrics, MC-dropout intervals and limitations; Figs. 5-8 and clinician case studies evaluate the interface.
reviewer_b_anchors: Accepted manuscript Sections 3-5, quantitative evaluation tables, DITTO workflow/interface figures, two case studies, and Appendix A.2; temporal outputs are shown at 12/24/36/48 months and to 5 years; MC dropout uses at least 20 samples; propensity matching requires at least 5 comparators within a caliper; formative work involved 11 physicians.

reviewer_a_notes: Held-out animals are adapted through data assimilation, so external evidence is 1 rather than frozen validation. title: Simulating the outcome of amyloid treatments in Alzheimer's disease from imaging and clinical data.
reviewer_a_notes: Action evidence is strong because dose and timing are explicitly perturbed against natural progression. Causal evidence remains partial: effects are generated from assumed ODE structure without treatment-confounding identification. Independent-cohort validation concerns disease severity rather than intervention response, and frozen status was not verifiable because the supplement was inaccessible. No code or hazard model.
reviewer_b_notes: The paper defines a clear no-treatment versus dose/timing intervention contrast, but no treated outcomes identify that contrast. Causal evidence is therefore partial: confounding, empirical overlap, and treatment-effect validation are unavailable. Long trajectories are generated, but performance degradation is not reported at multiple rollout horizons. No code, trained parameters, formal calibration, or safety model was found.
reviewer_a_anchors: PMC8168944 Methods: 442-person ADNI cohort, latent ODE and intervention definition; Figs. 3-7 and Table 2 compare placebo with 50%/100% lowering across intervention years and sample sizes; Discussion states a conditional causal interpretation and cautions about unmodeled mechanisms; supplement link could not be retrieved.
reviewer_b_anchors: Methods define 442 amyloid-positive ADNI participants/2,781 observations, irregular multimodal data, four coupled latent disease components, Gaussian decoders, and intervention simulation; Results figures compare natural history with 50%/100% amyloid lowering over intervention times and long disease-course trajectories; Discussion explicitly bounds conclusions as hypothetical model-based scenarios.

title: Towards Causality-Aware Inferring: A Sequential Discriminative Approach for Medical Diagnosis.
reviewer_a_notes: The method plans sequential inquiries in a simulator and defines individual potential symptom responses, but does not identify effects on real clinical outcomes. Cross-dataset transfer uses semantic remapping and is not frozen. Bootstrap confidence drives stopping without formal calibration; conservative stopping and human override are discussed without a clinical harm/severity test.
reviewer_b_notes: The closed loop is a short patient-simulator dialogue, not live clinical use. Matching and intervention-inspired masking address two observed inquiry biases but do not specify a causal treatment estimand or complete identification assumptions. Confidence thresholds and limited query budgets are safety-adjacent, not an explicit hazard test. Cross-dataset/OOD evidence is useful but not frozen institutional validation.
reviewer_a_anchors: arXiv:2003.06534v5 pp. 1-10, Tables 1-7 and Figs. 7-10 report counterfactual-answer metrics, closed-loop diagnosis, ablations, OOD and cross-dataset transfer; Appendix pp. 11-19 gives potential-outcome assumptions, training, human evaluation and limitations; CAMAD code is public.
reviewer_b_anchors: Methods define MZ (586/142; 66 symptoms/4 diseases) and DX (423/104; 41 symptoms/5 diseases), propensity latent matching, progressive assurance inquiry/diagnosis, Ptrain-to-Pall OOD evaluation, 1/3-symptom inquiry budgets, five-fold analysis, and five seeds; Results include matching/masking ablations, sequential diagnostic success, OOD comparisons, and six-physician blinded evaluation; official CAMAD repository provides code.
